domains.label: Performance
domains.objection: Cute syntax, slower than C or Rust.
domains.answer: Equivalent algorithms and semantics produce competitive native artifacts under hostile measurement.

domains.label: Compression
domains.objection: It is only syntax golf or generated boilerplate.
domains.answer: One semantic authority replaces duplicated facts, mechanisms, files, and projections.

domains.label: Dynamicity
domains.objection: The fast path quietly turned a dynamic language into a static one.
domains.answer: One source meaning moves from open dynamic execution through guarded and sealed native realizations.

domains.label: Metaprogramming
domains.objection: Existing macro and comptime systems already do this.
domains.answer: One ordinary semantic program derives implementation, tests, documentation, tooling, and foreign projections.

domains.label: Foreign leverage
domains.objection: Nobody will rewrite an existing project in an experimental language.
domains.answer: Imported foreign semantics improve an otherwise untouched project and regenerate deterministically.

domains.label: Systems credibility
domains.objection: Research languages collapse under substantial systems software.
domains.answer: Ward, native targets, and bootstrap stages work through the released compiler with explicit fallbacks.

domains.label: Trust
domains.objection: The claims are cherry-picked, generated, or secretly delegated to C.
domains.answer: Every release claim resolves to reproducible source, commands, artifacts, logs, and measurements.
